title: Pareus: acts of faith, fear and love dispose to sanctification
source_text: XXXI. Atque huc etiam facit quod inter Protestantes viri magni nominis agnoscunt esse quasdam dispositiones ad sanctificationem, quae vi spiritus Dei excitantur in hominibus sanctificandis & regenerandis; quales sunt actus varii, fidei, timoris, dilectionis, ut videre est apud Paraeum in librum 1. Bellarmini de Justificatione cap. 3. Actus autem fidei atque dilectionis non possunt non esse bona quaedam opera; quae cum supponantur esse dispositiones quaedam ad sanctificationem, sive regenerationem, non possunt etiam non illam quodammodo antecedere.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. And to this also tends that among the Protestants men of great name acknowledge that there are certain dispositions to sanctification, which by force of the spirit of God are excited in men to be sanctified and regenerated; such as are various acts, of faith, of fear, of love, as may be seen in Pareus on book 1 of Bellarmine on Justification chap. 3. But acts of faith and love cannot not be certain good works; which since they are supposed to be certain dispositions to sanctification, or regeneration, cannot also not in some way precede it.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXI. To the same point is the fact that Protestants of great name acknowledge certain dispositions to sanctification, aroused by the power of God's Spirit in people who are to be sanctified and regenerated. These are various acts of faith, fear and love, as can be seen in Pareus on Bellarmine's On justification, book 1, chapter 3.
Acts of faith and love cannot fail to be good works. And since they are taken to be dispositions to sanctification, or regeneration, they cannot fail to come before it in some way as well.
